simulators.name: AI2-THOR 5.0.0 (Unity)
simulators.definition: Native indoor simulator with rendered RGB, object interactions, visibility, navigation and collision.
simulators.evidence: Native software-rendering records on FloorPlan1/2/3; current live service has not been revalidated on a GPU.
variables: FloorPlan layout, start pose and sampled object bindings; only supported combinations are generated.
Movement, yaw and pitch; RGB reveals only the current view.
Native transforms, visibility, open/closed state, parent receptacles and one-hand inventory.
Limits interaction length; invalid actions consume budget.

simulators.name: Procedural Shape3D simulator
simulators.definition: Repository-local geometric simulator with voxel shapes, camera motion, object rotations and raster observations.
simulators.revision: Local task framework; per-build source hashes are recorded.
simulators.evidence: Recorded Oracle and model attempts; lightweight online reset/step checks use the actual simulator.
variables: Voxel arrangement, symmetry, candidate set or reference pose.
Position, yaw and pitch alter the observation, not the shape identity.
World-axis quarter turns; changed only by object-rotation actions.
Visibility and interaction limits; levels are structural, not policy-calibrated.

simulators.name: SimWorld — DeliveryBench gym_citynav build
simulators.definition: The dedicated SimWorld/Unreal package used by DeliveryBench. Delivery is a task layer; this executable supplies cities, rendering, movement and UnrealCV interaction.
simulators.revision: Package asset revision 64a4889d72a2c7b792d242083e53a926b43ceaa9; recorded engine UE 5.3.2-29314046.
simulators.evidence: interaction-demo-345795/simulator.log records the engine version and executed map. It is a separate package from 02_Simulator/SimWorld/Linux/. The standalone SimWorld source revision is not asserted to be this binary's source revision.
variables: Ten local city datasets; a live city change requires restarting the allocated UE process.
UE coordinates are centimetres; the native API also accepts metre-suffixed MOVE targets.
Global map, local map and first-person RGB are distinct named streams.
Read from native task-manager fields; diagram sliders do not alter simulator state.
Preparation/deadline, pickup/dropoff, temperature, carrying and placement constraints.

missing_object.definition: Spatial change detection: inspect an initial room, commit memory, then identify one hidden removal.
missing_object.objective: Identify the missing object and its previous receptacle. New native sessions ground references in observed image pixels; historical recordings used stable numeric IDs.
factors: One object's rendering, collision and interaction are deactivated after MEMORIZE.
The agent chooses views and writes its own memory before detection.
missing_object.verification: Check the submitted `answer.changes`: `object_id`, change `type` and `previous_location`. Strict success requires correct identity and prior location; `previous_location_accuracy` is separate from partial `reward`.
missing_object.difficulty: Implemented controls: L1 samples initially visible pickupable targets with bounding-box area at least 100 pixels; L2 permits smaller targets (8–1800 pixels) and changes the initial viewpoint after fixture selection. Missing-object L3 is not supported by the current native generator. `exploration_budget`, `max_steps`, target visibility and start pose govern evidence acquisition. `active_scan_v1` additionally requires target discovery outside the initial view and an explicit memory stage; this protocol has not been validated by these historical clips. Levels are structural, not measured policy difficulty.
missing_object.actions: Navigation and view actions; `MEMORIZE`; `SUBMIT` with a structured changes list.
missing_object.limits: Removal means native deactivation in this build. An individual view may occlude the changed object. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

moved_object.definition: Spatial change detection across viewpoints after one hidden object relocation.
moved_object.objective: Report the moved object and both its old and new receptacles.
factors: A collision-checked native placement changes the object's receptacle.
Camera movement is independent of object movement.
moved_object.verification: Verify `object_id`, change `type`, `previous_location` and `current_location`. All components must be correct for strict `success`.
moved_object.difficulty: L1/L2 target eligibility uses different image-area ranges; L2 resets the initial view. L3 is supported for moved-object. `exploration_budget`, `max_steps`, collision-checked destination and old/new receptacles determine search and memory requirements. Start visibility, relocation and the memory protocol must be inspected for the selected case; these controls are not a calibrated success hierarchy.
moved_object.limits: A correct object ID alone is insufficient; Oracle reports use privileged state. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

shape_identification.definition: Active 3D shape identification from chosen camera views and fixed candidate panels.
shape_identification.objective: Select the candidate with the same three-dimensional shape as the target.
factors: Camera movement changes the evidence; target identity is invariant.
shape_identification.verification: Compare submitted `candidate_id` to target identity. Report `shape_accuracy`; view count and action cost are separate diagnostics.
shape_identification.difficulty: Default construction uses `voxels = 5 + difficulty` and `candidates = min(5, 2 + difficulty)`; above L1 the initial cube orientation is sampled from 24 proper rotations. Default occlusion is 0 below L4 and 0.35 at L4+. Explicit task parameters override defaults. `require_initial_pixel_ambiguity` additionally demands a pixel-equivalent initial alternative and an informative reachable view. Historical examples do not establish that intervention or measured policy difficulty.
shape_identification.limits: This is a geometric simulator, not a photorealistic indoor scene.

pose_alignment.definition: Interactive object-pose alignment with independent camera and object transformations.
pose_alignment.objective: Rotate the target to match the reference orientation, accounting for object symmetry.
factors: Moving the camera does not rotate the target.
pose_alignment.verification: At `SUBMIT_POSE`, compute symmetry-aware `rotation_error_degrees`; the orientation must match within the evaluator tolerance.
pose_alignment.difficulty: Default shape size is `5 + difficulty` voxels. The reference is sampled at an exact symmetry-aware minimum depth of `min(difficulty, 3)` quarter turns over the allowed `axes` (3 is the cube-rotation diameter; restricted axes cap it at their deepest reachable pose; `alignment_length` overrides it). Earlier recordings used `1 + difficulty` random turns, whose minimum length did not grow with the level. Initial orientation and optional occlusion follow Shape3D controls. Strict evaluation uses symmetry-aware angular error; levels remain structural.
pose_alignment.limits: World-axis quarter turns are discrete; the task does not claim continuous robotic control.

memory_maze.definition: Indoor landmark exploration and ordered physical revisits in native AI2-THOR rooms.
memory_maze.objective: Visit and mark landmarks in the requested order, then finish near the last one.
factors: L1/L2/L3 request 2/4/5 visits, including revisits at higher levels.
MARK requires the object to be visible within 1.6 m.
memory_maze.verification: Check `ordered_visits` against `required_visits`, and require final proximity. `wrong_visits` and `environment_actions` diagnose the interaction history.
memory_maze.difficulty: L1/L2/L3 select 2/3/4 reachable landmarks; L2/L3 append a return to the first landmark, yielding 2/4/5 ordered visits. `MARK` requires visibility within 1.6 m. `exploration_budget`, `max_steps`, initial pose and `explicit_recall_v1` control acquisition and recall. The selected historical recording may start in recall; it does not establish a memory benefit.
memory_maze.limits: The native kitchen is not a literal maze. Exploration can sometimes be bypassed; no information-theoretic memory necessity is claimed. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

dependency_doors.definition: Physical container-access prerequisites and ordered object retrieval/delivery.
dependency_doors.objective: Open the source, retrieve and deliver requested objects, close used sources and finish empty-handed.
factors: Closed-source rejection and executable retrieval are checked during construction.
dependency_doors.verification: Verify ordered pickup/placement, `delivered` versus `required`, final receptacles, `sources_closed` and empty native inventory (`inventoryObjects`).
dependency_doors.difficulty: L1/L2/L3 request 1/2/3 verified container retrieval-and-delivery orders. Opening before pickup, placement in the target receptacle, restoring closure and ending empty-handed are conjunctive requirements. Cases with insufficient valid dependencies are rejected. Route length, occlusion and action budget add instance variation; empirical policy difficulty is uncalibrated.
dependency_doors.limits: This native task uses real containers, not the symbolic prototype's key/lock chain. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

relational_rearrangement.definition: Physical object rearrangement under world-frame spatial relations and preservation constraints.
relational_rearrangement.objective: Choose a valid placement for the target while preserving the anchor and all protected objects.
factors: Levels progress from one direction to direction/distance conjunctions.
Placement must be visible, unoccluded and within reach; screen axes do not define the relation.
relational_rearrangement.verification: Require `relation_satisfied`, `protected_objects_preserved` and `hand_empty`, with actual pickup and preservation of touch history.
relational_rearrangement.difficulty: L1 requires a signed relation along one axis. L2 retains one axis and adds a proximity bound (`near = 0.85 m`). L3 requires both x and z signed relations plus that proximity bound. Generation requires both valid and invalid candidate slots, and evaluation preserves protected objects and an empty final hand. Several placements can be valid; levels are not model-calibrated.
relational_rearrangement.limits: Single-target discrete placement; pose reasoning is handled separately. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

dynamic_replanning.definition: Navigation after a checkpoint-triggered physical obstruction changes the room.
dynamic_replanning.objective: Reach the checkpoint, find a valid detour, then mark and finish near the destination.
factors: A real object moves after the checkpoint is reached.
A formerly traversable edge must fail and an executable alternate route must remain.
dynamic_replanning.verification: Require `checkpoint_reached`, `goal_marked`, `at_goal` and `native_blocked_edge_verified`; the evaluator checks the physical intervention and completed navigation.
dynamic_replanning.difficulty: L1/L2/L3 require sampled routes of at least `8 + 2 × difficulty` nodes before the verified checkpoint intervention. A physical obstruction and executable detour are checked. One intervention is used; route length alone does not establish adaptation. Checkpoint visibility, detour and `max_steps` affect the selected instance. No measured hierarchy is claimed.
dynamic_replanning.limits: This is indoor physical replanning, not simulated road traffic. Native RGB no longer overlays object numbers. Public references use `view:STEP:X:Y` (normalized observed-image coordinates); segmentation and identifier resolution remain private. Existing clips use the previous numbered protocol. New native rollouts require runtime revalidation; ambiguous same-type textual goals are rejected.

deliverybench.definition: Long-horizon courier delivery task implemented by the DeliveryBench Python task layer on its dedicated SimWorld build.
deliverybench.objective: Complete deliveries and maximize net profit while respecting native spatial, time, resource and food-handling constraints.
factors: Pickup, preparation time, deadline and customer instructions.
Travel time, costs, stamina, battery and charging.
Temperature, compartment placement and delivery quality.
deliverybench.verification: Use native delivery lifecycle and settlement records. `_compute_reward()` in the Gym wrapper returns zero; `reward` alone is not net profit or a benchmark score.
deliverybench.difficulty: City size and task constraints are benchmark factors; there is no shared L1-L3 scale with the custom tasks.
deliverybench.limits: The imported eight-snapshot recording is a manual/scripted integration cutoff, not a successful full benchmark episode. Task wrapper revision af7146c9e09edc06137c2c9e330190a0a177fdc8.
